stories.title: PCCP, Stonemount Close on $1B-Plus Acquisition of Blackstone Industrial Portfolio
stories.excerpt: PCCP and Stonemount Financial Group are officially the new owners of a 5.9 million-square-foot industrial portfolio, Commercial Observer can first report. The joint venture acquired the 38 assets, located across 14 markets in 10 states, for upward of $1 billion with Blackstone as the seller, according to an article from Real Estate Alert preceding the sale. The portfolio was sold via an off-market transaction, with Eastdil Secured serving as adviser, and the transaction closed July 29. It wasn’t immediately clear how the acquisition was financed. “The acquisition of this portfolio represents PCCP’s continued conviction in the industrial sector and in markets we have actively invested in within the last five years,” Ryan Dodge, a partner with PCCP, said. “We believe our industrial portfolio continues to exhibit strong momentum, with increased leasing demand in recent months. In our view, this portfolio is well positioned to benefit from those same market tailwinds.” The portfolio — leased to a diverse roster of more than 70 tenants — is located across infill submarkets, including Denver, Dallas, Atlanta, and Charlotte, N.C., as well as strong growth markets like San Diego, Reno, Nev., and El Paso, Texas. With PCCP and Stonemount Financial now in the driver’s seat, the JV’s plan is to focus on revenue growth via contractual rent increases and marking-to-market on leases that are being renewed, according to a release. “This transaction reflects our conviction in the long-term fundamentals of the industrial real estate sector,” said Zack Markwell, CEO and managing principal at Stonemont. “We are pleased to have once again partnered with PCCP and will continue to pursue attractive acquisition opportunities alongside our active development program.” The industrial sector is one of PCCP’s investment fortés, with the firm currently managing more than 68 million square feet of industrial assets over 52 markets. This acquisition brings its count to 262 industrial transactions
bullets: PCCP and Stonemount acquire 5.9M SF industrial portfolio, 38 assets, 14 markets, $1B+ from Blackstone
Off-market transaction closed July 29; diverse tenant roster; portfolio leased across 10 states
PCCP cites strong leasing demand momentum and portfolio positioned for industrial market tailwinds
stories.summary: PCCP and Stonemount Financial Group closed a $1B-plus acquisition of a 38-asset, 5.9 million-square-foot industrial portfolio from Blackstone across 14 markets in 10 states, with the transaction closing July 29 via an off-market process. The portfolio is fully leased to a diverse tenant base. PCCP highlighted increased leasing demand in recent months as a key driver of conviction in the deal, signaling sustained momentum in the industrial sector.
stories.impact: Industrial capital remains active and liquid despite higher rates, with institutional buyers repositioning portfolios. This signals sustained investor confidence in logistics and distribution fundamentals—likely driven by e-commerce, nearshoring, and supply-chain diversification. Multifamily developers competing for land and construction capital in these same 14 markets may face tighter acquisition opportunities and faster land price appreciation in logistics-heavy submarkets.

stories.title: Fed Holds Interest Rates in Warsh’s Second Meeting as FOMC Chair
stories.excerpt: The second Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting under new Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh signaled another reality check of higher-for-longer interest rates to the commercial real estate industry. In a 9-3 vote, the FOMC maintained its benchmark interest rate Wednesday at between 3.5 percent and 3.75 percent for the fifth straight meeting, citing inflation risks from ongoing war in Iran. Inflation remains well above the Fed’s 2 percent target at a time when Warsh has laid the groundwork for possibly changing its data approach when crafting monetary policy decisions. Warsh said in a post-meeting press conference that the FOMC doesn’t have a “soft target” for inflation and remains committed to the 2 percent annual rate as a chief goal. “We have begun a new chapter and we understand that the five-plus years of inflation above target cannot be cured in nine weeks or by a single month of modest price decreases,” Warsh said. “This Fed will not waver. Our credibility rests on performing our duties and delivering on our responsibilities.” The vote to maintain interest rates came with some dissent as FOMC regional presidents Beth M. Hammack of Cleveland, Neel Kashkari of Minneapolis and Lorie K. Logan of Dallas voted no, preferring instead to implement a quarter-point hike. Warsh’s second meeting leading the Fed after replacing Jerome Powell as chair in May occurred two weeks after he said during congressional testimony that the FOMC has “no tolerance for persistently elevated inflation.” Warsh also spoke to whether traditional inflation gauges such as the Consumer Price Index and the Producer Price Index (PPI) should be rethought. The new Fed chair appointed a task force in June that will examine whether the central bank’s long-standing inflation metrics needs to change, with findings expected later in the year. bullets: Fed holds rates steady 3.5–3.75% for fifth consecutive meeting under Chair Kevin Warsh
9-3 vote reflects dissent; inflation above 2% target; Warsh signals commitment to long-term price stability

stories.summary: The Federal Reserve held its benchmark rate at 3.5–3.75% on Wednesday in a 9-3 vote, marking the fifth consecutive hold under new Chair Kevin Warsh. Warsh stated the Fed understands "five-plus years of inflation above target cannot be cured in nine weeks" and reaffirmed a commitment to the 2% inflation target. The decision signals persistence of elevated rates despite some dissent favoring a hike.
stories.impact: The Fed's "higher-for-longer" stance locks in elevated refinancing costs and construction financing rates for multifamily developers. Reduced leverage capacity, higher debt service on bridge and construction loans, and tighter equity returns will suppress starts and slow acquisitions in all metros through at least September's next meeting. Developers with rate locks or fixed-rate construction financing secured before this decision gain material competitive advantage.

stories.title: Two Hyatt Hotels Planned at Scottsdale-Area Indian Community
stories.excerpt: A Hyatt Place and a Hyatt Studios are slated to be built on Salt River Pima-Maricopa Indian land near Scottsdale along Loop 101. A groundbreaking was recently held for the Arizona Boardwalk Hyatt Place at Talking Stick (shown), a four-story, 142-room hotel that will be constructed adjacent to Arizona Boardwalk, the entertainment center home to a variety of attractions, including OdySea Aquarium, Butterfly Wonderland, Museum of Illusions and the Boardwalk Big Wheel. The Arizona Boardwalk Hyatt Place at Talking Stick will feature a lobby bar and lounge, breakfast and dining area, meeting space, fitness center and outdoor pool. The Hyatt Place project was designed by Deutsch Architecture Group and is being built by Layton Construction. It is projected to open in late 2027. Just south of the Arizona Boardwalk project, another Hyatt property, a Hyatt Studios hotel, has been proposed. It would be a four-story, 122-room extended stay hotel. The Hyatt Studios project is being proposed by CaliberCos Inc. The post Two Hyatt Hotels Planned at Scottsdale-Area Indian Community appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Hyatt Place 142 rooms, Hyatt Studios 122 rooms, both on Salt River Pima-Maricopa land, Scottsdale Loop 101
Hyatt Place groundbreaking held; four-story; opening late 2027; adjacent to Arizona Boardwalk entertainment center
Hyatt Studios proposed by CaliberCos; four-story extended-stay format; south of Arizona Boardwalk project
stories.summary: Two Hyatt hotels are under development on Salt River Pima-Maricopa Indian land in the Scottsdale area along Loop 101: a 142-room, four-story Hyatt Place designed by Deutsch Architecture Group and being built by Layton Construction (opening late 2027), and a proposed 122-room, four-story Hyatt Studios extended-stay property. The Hyatt Place is adjacent to Arizona Boardwalk, an entertainment venue housing OdySea Aquarium, Butterfly Wonderland, and other attractions.
stories.impact: Limited direct relevance to multifamily development. However, the extended-stay Hyatt Studios signals demand for flexible, longer-term lodging in the Scottsdale Loop 101 corridor—a potential canary for corporate relocation or seasonal workforce migration into the Phoenix metro. If this leisure-and-business-travel hub continues densifying, nearby multifamily developers should monitor job creation in hospitality, professional services, and tourism-adjacent industries to time residential deliveries ahead of sustained population inflow.

stories.title: MonticelloAM Closes $29M Transaction for Illinois Apartment Complex
stories.excerpt: MonticelloAM, along with a firm affiliate, closed a bridge loan for an apartment complex in McHenry, Illinois. The transaction was brought to MonticelloAM by Trent Niederberger of JLL Chicago. MonticelloAM Senior Managing Director Darryl Myrose worked with the JLL Chicago team on the origination of the transaction. “This transaction marks the beginning of a new partnership with an experienced Midwest sponsor, and we are excited to support their continued growth while expanding our presence alongside a proven operator in the region,” said Myrose. The loan carries a 24-month initial term with three 12-month extension options. Proceeds will be utilized to finance the acquisition of the property and allow the sponsor, Cunat Inc., a privately held real estate firm that owns and operates over 4,000 units in the Midwest, to execute on their renovation plan. The property, Fawn Ridge Apartments, is a garden-style multifamily property comprised of 208 units across nine buildings in northwest Chicago. The post MonticelloAM Closes $29M Transaction for Illinois Apartment Complex appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: MonticelloAM closes $29M bridge loan, McHenry, Illinois apartment complex, Fawn Ridge Apartments 208 units
24-month initial term, three 12-month extension options; borrower Cunat Inc. operates 4,000+ Midwest units
Proceeds fund acquisition and renovation; garden-style, nine buildings northwest Chicago submarket
stories.summary: MonticelloAM, alongside JLL Chicago, closed a $29 million bridge loan for the acquisition and renovation of Fawn Ridge Apartments, a 208-unit garden-style multifamily property in McHenry (northwest Chicago). The borrower, Cunat Inc., a privately held Midwest operator with 4,000+ units, will use proceeds to execute a capital plan. The loan carries a 24-month initial term with three 12-month extension options.
stories.impact: Bridge lending to value-add operators in secondary Midwest markets remains available, suggesting stable debt markets for re-capitalization plays. Cunat's continued expansion signals confidence in Chicago-area rent growth and renovation returns. For competing developers in northwest Chicago and McHenry, this indicates an active buyer pool for stabilized and near-stabilized assets, tightening secondary-market acquisition opportunities and pushing land prices higher for new development.

stories.title: Lincoln Property Company Acquires 275K-SF Puyallup Industrial Campus
stories.excerpt: JLL announced that Lincoln Property Company’s Logistics Fund II has acquired Canyon Road Commerce Center, a 275,000-square-foot industrial campus in Pierce County, Washington. As part of the acquisition, Lincoln has appointed JLL as the property’s exclusive leasing agent, launching a leasing initiative aimed at attracting advanced manufacturing, aerospace, logistics and distribution users across the South Sound. Canyon Road is the third acquisition for Lincoln Logistics Fund II. The fund has secured more than $280 million in capital commitments from two institutional investors, alongside Stone Point Capital and Lincoln employees. Leasing for Canyon Road will be led by JLL’s Chris Spofford, Bill Honsaker, Scott Carter and David Cahill. Located at 5103 136th Street E. in Puyallup, the property was acquired from Trammell Crow Company and an affiliate of CBRE Investment Management. “The Pacific Northwest continues to demonstrate the long-term fundamentals we seek as investors, including sustained population growth, a highly skilled workforce and a diverse industrial economy,” said Gary Kobus, Co-Head of Logistics and Senior Managing Director at Lincoln. The post Lincoln Property Company Acquires 275K-SF Puyallup Industrial Campus appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Lincoln Property Company Logistics Fund II acquires Canyon Road Commerce Center, 275K SF, Puyallup, Washington
Third acquisition for the fund; $280M+ capital commitments from institutional investors, Stone Point, Lincoln employees

stories.summary: Lincoln Property Company's Logistics Fund II has acquired Canyon Road Commerce Center, a 275,000-square-foot industrial campus in Puyallup (Pierce County, Washington), marking its third acquisition. The fund has secured $280M+ in capital commitments and targets advanced manufacturing, aerospace, logistics, and distribution tenants across the South Sound. The property was sold by Trammell Crow Company and a CBRE Investment Management affiliate.
stories.impact: Lincoln's continued institutional capital deployment into industrial assets signals sustained logistics/manufacturing demand in the Pacific Northwest. The South Sound (Tacoma/Puyallup) is a key corridor for aerospace, e-commerce, and regional distribution—demand drivers that also support multifamily growth. Developers in Puyallup and nearby Pierce County should expect tightening industrial land supply and rising land values, which could increase mixed-use development feasibility but also compete for scarce development-ready sites.

stories.title: Madison Realty Capital Leads $227M Refi of New Miami-Dade Rental
stories.excerpt: Baron Property Group (BPG) has secured $226.5 million to refinance a newly completed multifamily development in Hialeah, Fla. Madison Realty Capital and Yellowstone Real Estate provided the debt backing the 559-unit Metro Parc at 955 East 25th Street, about a block west of Metrorail and Tri-Rail transfer stations in a working-class area of Miami-Dade County. BPG completed the 10-story building last year after securing a $148 million construction loan from Post Road Group in 2022. The 754,016-square-foot project — which includes 15,000 square feet of retail space, partly leased to Cuban bakery Mr. Baker — is nearly 50 percent leased, according to a representative for the developer. The refinance will replace the project’s construction loan and will serve as a bridge to permanent financing. Ben Suky brokered the transaction. Metro Parc represents the first phase of Baron Property Group’s 2.3 million-square-foot residential development. The second phase, called Metro Parc North and adjacent to Metro Parc, recently topped out and is scheduled to be completed in late 2027. Post Road Group provided a $206 million construction loan for that phase last year. MG Developer, an original partner in both Metro Parc projects, is no longer involved, per a representative for BPG, who has not provided additional details. MG Developer is currently building the 347-unit Metro Parc South across the street after landing a $105 million construction loan last year. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Baron Property Group secures $226.5M refinance, Madison Realty Capital and Yellowstone Real Estate, Metro Parc Hialeah
559-unit, 10-story, 754K SF, nearly 50% leased at stabilization; includes 15K SF retail (Mr. Baker anchor)
Bridge to permanent; replaced $148M construction loan; Phase 2 (Metro Parc North) recently topped out
stories.summary: Baron Property Group has secured a $226.5 million refinance led by Madison Realty Capital and Yellowstone Real Estate for Metro Parc, a newly completed 559-unit, 10-story development in Hialeah near Metrorail and Tri-Rail stations. The project, 754,016 square feet with 15,000 SF of retail, is nearly 50% leased and replaces the original $148 million construction loan. The refinance serves as a bridge to permanent financing; Phase 2 (Metro Parc North) has recently topped out.
stories.impact: Strong refinance execution at 50% occupancy signals healthy debt markets for transit-oriented multifamily in Miami-Dade despite higher rates. Proximity to Metrorail/Tri-Rail and retail anchors demonstrates lender comfort with mixed-use, transit-connected value-add products. For competing developers in Miami-Dade, this validates demand for workforce housing in transit corridors and shows refinance windows open before stabilization—enabling earlier capital recovery and follow-on Phase 2/3 starts.

stories.title: Fed Holds Rates Steady Despite Dissenting Voices
stories.excerpt: The Federal Reserve voted to hold its benchmark interest rate steady at 3.5% to 3.75% on Wednesday, maintaining the policy target range established in January. The decision was not unanimous, as three central bank officials dissented in favor of a quarter-point rate increase: Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack, Minneapolis Fed President Neel Kashkari, and Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan. The hold puts an end to pre-meeting speculation that policymakers might move to raise rates. Expectations for a hike had been driven by views that Fed Chair Kevin Warsh would look to reinforce his inflation-fighting credentials early in his tenure. By leaving borrowing costs unchanged, the Federal Open Market Committee now shifts market attention to its upcoming policy meeting in September. The post Fed Holds Rates Steady Despite Dissenting Voices appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Fed holds rates 3.5–3.75%; three officials (Hammack, Kashkari, Logan) dissent, favoring 0.25% hike

stories.summary: The Federal Reserve voted to hold its benchmark rate at 3.5–3.75%, with three dissenters (Cleveland's Beth Hammack, Minneapolis's Neel Kashkari, and Dallas's Lorie Logan) advocating for a quarter-point increase. The hold maintains the policy target established in January and redirects market focus to September's next meeting, ending pre-meeting speculation that Chair Kevin Warsh might signal early rate hikes to cement inflation-fighting credentials.
stories.impact: Growing Fed dissent signals emerging hawkish pressure, which could materialize as a rate hike by September. Multifamily borrowers should lock in construction and refinance financing now while rates remain at 3.5–3.75%, as any increase will compress underwriting returns and reduce deal feasibility. Developers with September closings should accelerate financing applications to avoid refinancing in a higher-rate environment.

stories.title: BXP Closes $1.2B Construction Loan for Madison Avenue Office Tower
stories.excerpt: BXP, Inc. has closed a $1.2-billion construction loan for the development of 343 Madison Ave., a planned 46-story, approximately 930,000-square-foot office tower in Midtown Manhattan with direct access to Grand Central Terminal’s Madison Concourse. The Boston-based REIT expects to complete the $2-billion project, currently about 50% pre-leased, in 2029. The construction loan facility has a four-year initial term, plus a one-year extension option subject to customary conditions. It was completed on highly competitive terms, including an initial interest rate of Term SOFR plus 2.50%, which will be reduced to Term SOFR plus 2.25% subject to certain leasing and construction milestones. “We are pleased to complete this financing, which reflects the quality of 343 Madison Ave., continued confidence in BXP’s development platform, and our ability to secure attractive financing terms in today’s market,” said Mike LaBelle, EVP, CFO, BXP. The financing was led by Wells Fargo Bank as administrative agent; BofA Securities, The Bank of New York Mellon Corporation and JPMorgan Chase Bank as joint lead arrangers; Banco Bilbao Vizcaya Argentaria, Landesbank Baden-Wurttemberg, PNC Bank and U.S. Bank as documentation agents; and BBVA as sustainability agent. Legal counsel was provided by Fried Frank for BXP and Riemer Braunstein for Wells Fargo. The post BXP Closes $1.2B Construction Loan for Madison Avenue Office Tower appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: BXP closes $1.2B construction loan, 343 Madison Ave., 46-story, 930K SF office tower, Midtown Manhattan
Four-year initial + one-year extension; Term SOFR + 2.50% (stepping to 2.25% on milestones); 50% pre-leased
Wells Fargo, BofA, BNY Mellon, JPMorgan as lead arrangers; $2B total project cost; completion 2029
stories.summary: BXP has closed a $1.2 billion construction loan for 343 Madison Avenue, a planned 46-story, 930,000-square-foot office tower in Midtown Manhattan with direct Grand Central access. The facility features a four-year initial term plus one-year extension, with rates at Term SOFR + 2.50% (stepping to 2.50% based on leasing/construction milestones). The $2 billion project is 50% pre-leased; completion is expected in 2029.
stories.impact: Large-dollar office construction financing at SOFR + 2.50% reflects strong institutional debt appetite for prime Manhattan assets with marquee tenants (C.V. Starr, McDermott Will & Schulte) and near-term delivery certainty. However, this demonstrates capital concentration in trophy office product. Multifamily developers in Manhattan and other major metros should note that institutional lenders remain selective and require substantial pre-leasing/anchor tenant commitments—raising barriers to entry for speculative or secondary-market residential starts.

stories.title: CBRE Reports Strong Q2 Earnings Amid Data Center Revenues, Office Leasing Gains
stories.excerpt: Surging data center services revenue and a rebound in U.S. office leasing stood out in CBRE’s strong second-quarter results for 2026. During a Wednesday morning earnings call, the world’s largest commercial real estate services and investment firm reported $11.2 billion in second-quarter revenue, roughly in line with analysts’ estimates. Revenue grew annually by 15.5 percent, and increased over its first-quarter results by roughly 6.6 percent. CBRE’s earnings beat analysts’ expectations, with core earnings per share of $1.56. Adjusted profit rose to $459 million from $361 million a year earlier, stripping out one-off line items like fire-safety repairs on U.K. buildings. The firm’s second-quarter report included more than $700 million in revenue from data center services. U.S. office leasing notched a second-quarter record, too, in a welcome signal of continued commercial recovery. CBRE’s more volatile segments, like property sales, mortgage origination and leasing, saw revenue growth of 19 percent year-over-year. U.S. leasing revenues spiked by 24 percent, led by office and industrial activity. Most notably, U.S. office leasing generated its highest-ever second-quarter revenue, according to Emma Giamartino, CBRE’s chief financial officer. The strength was driven by gateway markets, as well as space upgrades from financial and legal tenants. CBRE’s global property sales saw increased revenues of 20 percent, with the U.S. tracking a 24 percent increase across most property types. Despite the strong performance, there’s still room for recovery. “On the leasing side, we’re still not back to 2019 levels,” Giamartino said. “We see there’s more room to go this year, and that will extend into next year. And on the sales side, we’re still pretty early. bullets: CBRE reports Q2 2026 revenue $11.2B, up 15.5% YoY; core EPS $1.56, beating expectations
Data center services revenue exceeded $700M; U.S. office leasing hit second-quarter record; leasing revenue up 24% YoY

stories.summary: CBRE reported strong Q2 2026 results with $11.2 billion in revenue (up 15.5% YoY), core EPS of $1.56, and adjusted profit of $459 million (up from $361 million YoY). Data center services generated over $700 million in revenue, while U.S. office leasing reached a second-quarter record. U.S. leasing revenues surged 24% YoY, driven by office and industrial activity.
stories.impact: CBRE's outsized data center and office leasing growth signals capital and tenant demand flowing toward tech, AI infrastructure, and corporate real estate in core markets. This capital concentration in office and logistics may leave fewer institutional lenders and brokers focused on multifamily. Multifamily developers should expect rising brokerage fees, longer leasing timelines, and tighter competitive positioning for debt and equity capital relative to data center and prime office projects in 2026–2029.

stories.title: BXP Secures $1.2B Construction Loan for 343 Madison Avenue Office Tower
stories.excerpt: BXP, the largest Class A office owner in the country, has landed a $1.2 billion construction loan to build its 930,000-square-foot office tower development at 343 Madison Avenue in Midtown, the real estate investment trust (REIT) announced Wednesday morning during its second-quarter earnings call. The financing for BXP’s 46-story development came from Wells Fargo, Bank of America Securities, Bank of New York Mellon and J.P. Morgan Chase. The loan has a four-year initial term, plus a one-year extension option, according to BXP. Once construction is completed — a finish date is set for 2029 — the $2 billion project at 343 Madison Avenue will feature offices, dining spaces, terraces and plenty of amenities. The anticipated tower just west of Grand Central Terminal is also already 50 percent pre-leased, after insurance and investment giant C.V. Starr signed a 275,000-square-foot deal in October to anchor the property, and law firm McDermott Will & Schulte took roughly 150,000 square feet there in April. Starr later expanded its initial lease by another two full floors. BXP executives said during Wednesday’s earnings call that the firm is in negotiations with two more prospective tenants, which would bring the building to nearly 70 percent pre-leased. CEO Owen Thomas said the REIT will lease the rest of the floors closer to delivery to secure “market-leading rents.” “The pricing power in Manhattan remains quite favorable to landlords, and it is expanding geographically,” Hilary Spann, executive vice president of BXP’s New York region, said during the call. “We are getting inbound interest at our highest-quality buildings and at 343 Madison at rents that are consistently 10 to 15 percent above where they were last year. … And, in the lower stack of our buildings where rents are slightly more affordable, we’re still seeing 20 percent increases year-over-year, and that is fundamentally because there’s a lack of available space in the market. Same implication: prime Manhattan office construction attracts institutional capital, but bar for multifamily remains higher. Developers targeting Manhattan multifamily should recognize that office capital is flowing toward trophy assets with megadeals and high barriers to entry—creating a relative scarcity of financing for residential and emphasizing the need for strong sponsors, pre-leasing, and market differentiation.
